For constant \(q\), clipping produces a constant input to a scalar EMA, whose closed form and limit are exact. The clipping phase boundaries follow by solving two elementary reciprocal inequalities. The embedded verifier replays all identities independently.

value.rationale: Eve's distinctive contribution is its objective-driven global learning-rate adaptation. The exact reciprocal symmetry shows that the stabilized channel discards the sign of multiplicative progress: reciprocal improvement and worsening receive identical feedback. The geometric-trace phase diagram translates Eve's clipping hyperparameter into sharp, interpretable objective-gap thresholds and shows that faster monotone improvement systematically receives no larger asymptotic global rate. This is a natural structural diagnostic of the defining mechanism, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
